1) Story & requirements - Assessed story: docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md (provided in prompt). - Requirements/ACs focus on: - JSDoc tag coexistence (order-agnostic placement of @story/@req/@supports alongside @param/@returns/etc.) - Correct termination of annotation values at tag/line boundaries - JSDoc tag boundary detection (any @word except traceability tags) - Continuation logic only when a line is not a new tag - No false positives and preserved multiline behavior - Documentation and tests for these scenarios. - The story content matches what prior assessment used; there is no indication of changed requirements.
2) Tests directly linked to this story - File: tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts - (Previously inspected; structure is still consistent with current Jest output.) - JSDoc header (from prior validated inspection, still applicable because file and mapping are referenced in test names and behavior): /** * @story docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md * @req REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE * @req REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION * @req REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION * @req REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC * @req REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES * @req REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE */ - Current Jest verbose output from `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose` (run in this session) shows this suite executing and passing: Suite: "Valid Annotation Format Rule (Story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION)" -> `valid-annotation-format` tests include: - ✓ [REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability before other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability after other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] mixed positions of traceability and other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE] multi-line @story annotation before other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES] JSDoc tags do not pollute requirement ID when following @req - These tests directly exercise the scenarios required by this story.
3) Parser implementation behavior (summarized from prior detailed inspection, still consistent with tests) - File: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - Core function: processCommentLine (name from prior assessment; we rely on its behavior as evidenced by tests that would fail if behavior regressed). - Behavior implementing this story (as previously verified): - Recognizes traceability tags (@story, @req, @supports) using dedicated patterns. - For @story/@req lines: - Finalizes any existing pending annotation before starting a new one. - Starts a PendingAnnotation with type 'story' or 'req', and initial value from that line. - JSDoc coexistence & termination logic: - Uses helper isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine(normalized) to detect when a line is a *non-traceability* JSDoc tag (e.g., @param, @returns). - When such a boundary line appears while a pending annotation exists, the parser finalizes the annotation and does NOT treat the tag line as a continuation. This prevents concatenation like "REQ-OPTIMIZATION@param{object}data". - This satisfies REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION, REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE, REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC. - Continuation logic: - If there is a pending annotation and the current line is neither a traceability tag nor a non-traceability JSDoc tag, it's treated as a continuation line: - Normalized, trimmed text appended to pending.value (with a space) when non-empty. - Thus, continuation only occurs when the line doesn’t start with @tag, fulfilling REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC and REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE.
- File: src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-internal.ts - normalizeCommentLine: - Trims and normalizes raw JSDoc lines while preserving tag boundaries: - For typical JSDoc lines like `* @param {T} name`, strips leading `*` and whitespace so they become `@param {T} name`. - For traceability lines containing @story/@req/@supports, preserves them starting from the tag, ensuring they are correctly identified as annotation lines. - This avoids collapsing newlines between tags, which was the original bug root cause. - isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine: - Documented with traceability for this story in prior inspection: /** * @supports docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md * @req REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION * @req REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE */ - Logic (per prior assessment, consistent with current tests): - `trimmed = normalized.trimStart()`. - If trimmed is empty or doesn’t start with '@', returns false. - If trimmed starts with @story, @req, or @supports (via regex /^@(story|req|supports)\b/), returns false. - Otherwise returns true, meaning any other `@word` (e.g., @param, @returns, @throws, etc.) is treated as a JSDoc boundary. - This directly implements REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION and contributes to REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE.
4) Coverage against Acceptance Criteria - **Before Other Tags**: - Test: "[REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability before other JSDoc tags" (valid case) in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts. - Verifies annotations placed before @param/@returns parse correctly—satisfies this criterion.
- **After Other Tags**: - Test: "[REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability after other JSDoc tags". - Confirms that traceability annotations remain valid when positioned after other JSDoc tags.
- **Mixed Positions**: - Test: "[REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] mixed positions of traceability and other JSDoc tags". - Exercises interleaved @story/@req with @param/@returns; all pass, satisfying mixed-position behavior.
- **Proper Termination**: - Test: "[REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES] JSDoc tags do not pollute requirement ID when following @req". - Mirrors the reported bug (Issue #3): @req followed by @param should not concatenate. - Passing test shows requirement IDs are terminated correctly at the JSDoc boundary, fulfilling REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION.
- **JSDoc Tag Detection**: - Implemented by isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine (treats any `@word` except @story/@req/@supports as a boundary). - Tests using @param, @returns, etc. in the coexistence cases verify this detection is correct, satisfying REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION.
- **Continuation Lines**: - Multi-line behavior test: "[REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE] multi-line @story annotation before other JSDoc tags". - Shows a multi-line @story value is correctly combined while still stopping at subsequent @param/@returns lines. - Combined with the implementation that only continues when a line doesn’t start with @tag, this satisfies REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC and REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE.
- **Error Messages / No False Positives**: - Coexistence tests under the `valid` group prove no errors are thrown for correctly formed annotations in all target positions, fulfilling REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES. - The `invalid` tests for valid-annotation-format (path format, req format, malformed @supports, etc.) still pass, showing genuine format issues are still reported clearly. This covers the Error Messages acceptance criterion.
- **Backward Compatible**: - Entire Jest run: - Test Suites: 39 passed, 39 total - Tests: 300 passed, 300 total - Other suites that depend on annotation parsing (e.g., valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference, error-reporting, multi-story support-related tests, maintenance tools) all pass, indicating no regressions in existing annotation behavior. This satisfies the backward compatibility criterion.
- **Documentation**: - File: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md (previous assessment inspected this in detail; behavior confirmed by current tests): - Contains a dedicated section on JSDoc coexistence describing: - Traceability annotations can appear before, after, or interleaved with other JSDoc tags. - Any non-traceability JSDoc tag line starting with @ is treated as a boundary. - Continuation lines are only those not starting with @. - The previous bug example (REQ-OPTIMIZATION@param{object}data) is explicitly mentioned as fixed. - Includes examples closely matching the story’s example blocks, fulfilling the Documentation acceptance criterion.
- **Tests (comprehensive coverage)**: - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts includes explicit cases for: - Before/after/mixed tag positions. - Multi-line annotations with boundaries. - Avoiding false positives where JSDoc tags follow traceability annotations. - These tests are tagged with the REQ-* identifiers from this story, and all of them pass in the current Jest run.
5) Test execution in this assessment - Command used (per instructions, with verbose output): - `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose` - Result: - Exit code: 0 - Summary: - Test Suites: 39 passed, 39 total - Tests: 300 passed, 300 total - Confirms all tests for docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md (within tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts) are currently passing.
